newsitem.title: BELGIUM: IGC may have to consider budget.
newsitem.headline: IGC may have to consider budget.

text.p: Inter-governmental conference negotiators may have to reconsider the way that the European Union budget is handled following this week's IGC meeting, the group's chairman Noel Dorr has said.
At a news conference on Tuesday, Dorr said that most negotiators had favoured the status quo when it came to the budget but that two new proposals had been offered during the meetng on Tuesday.
One delegation proposed introducing something akin to co-decision, Dorr said, while another suggested having only one reading of the budget instead of two.
"We will have to come back to it," he said.
Dorr said he had spent Monday discussing the IGC with individual delegations.
"It was simply a way of ensuring we (the Irish presidency) are in touch with the positions of delegations," he said.
The Tuesday IGC meeting discussed five issues: institutions, the budget, the role of national parliaments, transparency and subsidiarity.
Dorr said that a good deal of support had emerged in the negotiations for strengthening the role of the European Commission president. As usual, the problem was how to do it.
Some discussion centered on the idea of having the European Parliament vote on the president -- which it now does off its own bat but with no legal basis behind it.
